q: Normally, atoms have equal numbers of electrons and protons so the net (overall) charge on a material is ____.
e: Normally, atoms have equal numbers of electrons and protons so the net (overall) charge on a material is zero. The physics in this sentence is built around zero.

q: However, when the two insulating materials are rubbed together, electrons may be ____ from one to the other.
e: However, when the two insulating materials are rubbed together, electrons may be transferred from one to the other. The physics in this sentence is built around transferred.

q: If two uncharged objects are rubbed with one another both of them become ____.
e: If two uncharged objects are rubbed with one another both of them become charged. The physics in this sentence is built around charged.

q: This is also called charging by ____.
e: This is also called charging by friction. Friction names this is also called charging by.

q: It is important that the rubbing does not produce or create charges but removes electrons from one object and ____ them to the other.
e: It is important that the rubbing does not produce or create charges but removes electrons from one object and transfers them to the other. The physics in this sentence is built around transfers.

q: As shown when a glass rod is rubbed with a silk cloth, the glass rod becomes ____ charged and the silk cloth negatively charged.
e: As shown when a glass rod is rubbed with a silk cloth, the glass rod becomes positively charged and the silk cloth negatively charged. The physics in this sentence is built around positively.

q: This is because some electrons of the glass rod are transferred to the ____ cloth.
e: This is because some electrons of the glass rod are transferred to the silk cloth. The physics in this sentence is built around silk.

q: Hence, the glass rod loses electrons while the silk cloth ____ electrons.
e: Hence, the glass rod loses electrons while the silk cloth gains electrons. The physics in this sentence is built around gains.

q: As another example, when a plastic rod is rubbed with fur, the plastic rod possesses a negative charge while the fur becomes ____ charged.
e: As another example, when a plastic rod is rubbed with fur, the plastic rod possesses a negative charge while the fur becomes positively charged. The physics in this sentence is built around positively.

q: Induction is the process of charging a conductor without any ____ with the charged body.
e: Induction is the process of charging a conductor without any contact with the charged body. A conductor has plenty of free electrons, so charge can move.

q: A charged object can attract ____ objects.
e: A charged object can attract uncharged objects. The physics in this sentence is built around uncharged.

q: The law of conservation of electric charge is one of the ____ laws.
e: The law of conservation of electric charge is one of the fundamental laws. The physics in this sentence is built around fundamental.

q: That is 'The net electric charge in an isolated system remains ____'.
e: That is 'The net electric charge in an isolated system remains constant'. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: The net charge is the ____ sum of the charges in an isolated system.
e: The net charge is the algebraic sum of the charges in an isolated system. The physics in this sentence is built around algebraic.

q: For example, in the experiment on electrification by stroking the glass rod with a silk cloth, they together form an ____ system.
e: For example, in the experiment on electrification by stroking the glass rod with a silk cloth, they together form an isolated system. The physics in this sentence is built around isolated.

q: There is no charge transfer between the surrounding and the ____ system.
e: There is no charge transfer between the surrounding and the isolated system. The physics in this sentence is built around isolated.

q: The net charge of isolated system remains constant before and after ____.
e: The net charge of isolated system remains constant before and after stroking. The physics in this sentence is built around stroking.
